documents.title: Mission and Theory of Change
documents.content:
# Mission and Theory of Change

## Mission
Cedar Ridge Veterans Collaborative helps veterans in the San Antonio region secure stable housing, rebuild connection with fellow veterans, and enter skilled-trades careers that sustain their families. We were founded in 2012 and serve Bexar County, with outreach in Comal and Guadalupe counties.

## The problem
Veterans who lose housing often face several pressures at once: a job loss, a disability, isolation after leaving service, or a family crisis. Services that address only one of these pressures tend to produce short-lived results.

## Theory of change
If veterans at risk of homelessness receive rapid housing navigation, structured peer support from other veterans, and a paid pathway into the skilled trades, then they will stay housed, reconnect with their community, and earn wages that keep their households stable. Housing, connection and employment are addressed together because a gap in any one of them puts the other two at risk.

## Principles
- Housing first: no preconditions for help with housing.
- Veteran-led: peer mentors are veterans themselves.
- Measured: outcomes are verified 6 and 12 months after exit.

documents.title: Programme Descriptions
documents.content:
# Programme Descriptions

## Homeward Navigation
Housing navigation, rapid rehousing and short-term rental assistance for veteran households at risk of or experiencing homelessness. Caseworkers work weekdays from our San Antonio office and in veterans' homes across Bexar County. Support includes landlord negotiation, security deposits, move-in costs and up to six months of rental assistance.

## Battle Buddy Peer Network
Trained veteran peer mentors lead weekly peer-support groups and one-to-one check-ins at our East Side centre and two partner sites. The network is supported by 48 volunteer peer mentors, each completing 24 hours of training before matching.

## Trades Forward
A 14-week skilled-trades pre-apprenticeship in electrical, HVAC and welding, run in three cohorts a year at our East Side training workshop. Participants earn industry-recognised safety certifications and are placed into registered apprenticeships with partner employers. Twenty-two volunteer trades mentors support the cohorts.

## How the programmes connect
Every veteran housed through Homeward Navigation is offered a peer mentor and a Trades Forward assessment.

documents.title: 2025-26 Impact Report
documents.content:
# 2025-26 Impact Report

## Who we served
- 1,100 veterans and family members served in total.
- 38% of veterans have a service-connected disability rating; 41% of households include children; 16% are women veterans.
- 57% identify as Hispanic/Latino, 19% as Black, 20% as white and 4% as another race or multiracial.

## Outcomes
- Homeward Navigation: 318 of 412 enrolled veteran households (77%) moved into permanent housing, an average of 38 days after enrolment.
- 87% of households housed in 2024-25 remained stably housed 12 months later.
- Battle Buddy Peer Network: 540 veterans took part; 72% reported lower loneliness on the UCLA Loneliness Scale after 12 weeks.
- Trades Forward: 118 of 146 participants (81%) completed training and 94 entered registered apprenticeships at an average starting wage of $21.40 an hour.

## In their words
"My caseworker found us an apartment in five weeks, and my peer mentor talked me into the HVAC cohort. I start my apprenticeship on Monday." — Army veteran and father of two

## How we measure
Outcomes are tracked in our HMIS-compatible case-management system and verified at 6 and 12 months after exit.

documents.title: FY2026 Budget Summary
documents.content:
# FY2026 Budget Summary

Annual operating budget (FY2026, year ending September 30, 2026): $3.1 million.

## Expenses
- Housing navigation and rapid rehousing staff: $820,000
- Rental and move-in assistance paid to landlords: $760,000
- Battle Buddy Peer Network: $310,000
- Trades Forward instructors, tools and certification fees: $540,000
- Administration and finance: $390,000
- Fundraising: $280,000
- Total: $3,100,000

## Revenue mix
- Federal government (direct veteran rapid rehousing grant): 42%
- Foundations: 26%
- State and local government: 12%
- Individual donors: 10%
- Corporate gifts: 8%
- Events: 2%

## Notes
Programme expenses (housing, peer support and Trades Forward) total $2,430,000, or 78% of the budget. The federal rapid rehousing grant provides $1,300,000 per year through 2027.

documents.title: Governance and Capacity
documents.content:
# Governance and Capacity

## Board
A 13-member board of directors, 7 of whom are veterans, meets every other month. Committees cover finance and audit, programmes, and governance. The board approves the annual budget and reviews outcomes each quarter.

## Staff and volunteers
31 full-time and 6 part-time staff, supported by 48 volunteer peer mentors and 22 volunteer trades mentors.

## Key leaders
- Dr. Marisol Vega-Hartley, Executive Director: a Navy veteran who has led the Collaborative since 2017.
- Terrence Okafor, Director of Housing Programmes: oversees Homeward Navigation and the federal rapid rehousing grant.
- Lauren Pruitt, Grants and Development Manager: manages 14 active grants and all funder reporting.

## Financial management
Independent audit, clean opinion, including a single audit of federal funds, for FY2025. A three-person grants and finance team conducts monthly budget-to-actual reviews. We have managed a direct federal award since 2019.

## Policies
Conflict of interest, whistleblower, document retention, client confidentiality and fair housing policies are approved by the board and reviewed every two years.

documents.title: Organisation Overview
documents.content:
# Organisation Overview (approved language)

Cedar Ridge Veterans Collaborative helps veterans in the San Antonio region secure stable housing, rebuild connection with fellow veterans, and enter skilled-trades careers that sustain their families. Since 2012 we have combined three programmes: Homeward Navigation, which provides housing navigation and rapid rehousing; the Battle Buddy Peer Network, which pairs veterans with trained veteran peer mentors; and Trades Forward, a 14-week pre-apprenticeship in electrical, HVAC and welding. In 2025-26, 318 veteran households moved into permanent housing, and 94 veterans entered registered apprenticeships. We manage a direct federal rapid rehousing grant and hold a clean independent audit.

opportunities.raw_text:
Lone Star Veterans Fund — Housing Stability for Texas Veterans (FICTIONAL SAMPLE)
The Fund invites Texas-based 501(c)(3) organisations with at least three years of experience serving veterans to apply for one-year grants of $50,000 to $150,000. Priority is given to housing navigation and rapid rehousing programmes that move veterans and their families into permanent housing and track retention after 12 months. Applicants that link housing with employment or peer support are especially encouraged. Funds may cover staff, rental and move-in assistance, and programme costs. The Fund does not support emergency shelter beds or capital construction. No match is required. Applications are due in six days and must include four narrative responses, a programme budget, the most recent audit and a board list. Grantees submit an interim report at six months and a final report with housing retention data at twelve months.

questions.prompt: Describe the need in your community and your organisation's approach to addressing it.
questions.answer: Cedar Ridge Veterans Collaborative is the leading veteran housing provider in Texas. Veteran homelessness is a really big problem and we work very hard every day to solve it. Our programmes have housed over 500 veterans last year, with nearly 100% of them staying housed. We take a holistic, wraparound, best-in-class approach that changes lives. We also help veterans find good jobs. With your support we can do even more to end veteran homelessness once and for all across the state.

Priority populations include veterans, people re-entering the workforce and adults with disabilities. The Foundation does not pay tuition to for-profit schools or provide general operating support. questions.prompt: Describe the training programme and the population it serves.
questions.answer: Trades Forward is a 14-week skilled-trades pre-apprenticeship in electrical, HVAC and welding, run in three cohorts a year at our East Side training workshop in San Antonio. Participants earn industry-recognised safety certifications and are placed into registered apprenticeships with partner employers, supported by 22 volunteer trades mentors. Every participant is a veteran. Across the households we serve, 38% of veterans have a service-connected disability rating, 41% of households include children and 16% are women veterans. Veterans housed through our Homeward Navigation programme are offered a Trades Forward assessment, so training builds directly on housing stability.

Outcomes are tracked in our HMIS-compatible case-management system and verified at 6 and 12 months after exit. A three-person grants and finance team reviews programme budgets against actual spending each month, and the board reviews outcomes each quarter.

questions.prompt: Why is your organisation well positioned to do this work?
questions.answer: Cedar Ridge Veterans Collaborative has served veterans in the San Antonio region since 2012 and addresses housing, peer connection and employment together. Homeward Navigation provides housing navigation and rapid rehousing; the Battle Buddy Peer Network pairs veterans with trained veteran peer mentors; and Trades Forward offers a 14-week pre-apprenticeship in electrical, HVAC and welding. In 2025-26, 318 of 412 enrolled veteran households (77%) moved into permanent housing, an average of 38 days after enrolment, and 87% of households housed in 2024-25 remained stably housed 12 months later. Of 146 Trades Forward participants, 94 entered registered apprenticeships at an average starting wage of $21.40 an hour. Our capacity is established: we have managed a direct federal rapid rehousing grant since 2019, hold an independent audit with a clean opinion, and are governed by a 13-member board, 7 of whom are veterans.

questions.prompt: How would general operating support strengthen your organisation?

Flexible support would strengthen the shared functions that hold our three programmes together: administration and finance ($390,000 in FY2026), the coordination that offers every veteran housed through Homeward Navigation a peer mentor and a Trades Forward assessment, and the outcome verification we carry out 6 and 12 months after exit. Unrestricted funding would also help us diversify a revenue mix in which foundations provide 26% and individual donors 10%, reducing reliance on any one source.

program_report.title: Programme Progress Report: August 1 – October 31, 2026
program_report.content:
# Programme Progress Report: August 1 – October 31, 2026

## Veteran Housing Stability Fund — Homeward Navigation

Mission City Community Foundation's $75,000 grant supports caseworker time and rental and move-in assistance for veteran households in Bexar County. This report covers the first quarter of the grant period (figures to October 20, 2026).

## Delivered so far
- 58 veteran households enrolled in Homeward Navigation with support from this grant.
- 41 households (71%) moved into permanent housing, an average of 36 days after enrolment.
- 17 households are still working with a caseworker on landlord negotiation or move-in.
- 24 of the 58 households (41%) include children; 22 veterans (38%) have a service-connected disability rating.
- 39 of the 41 newly housed veterans accepted a Battle Buddy peer mentor, and 12 completed a Trades Forward assessment.

## In their words
"I had a deposit and nowhere to use it until my caseworker sat down with the landlord. We moved in three weeks later." — Marine Corps veteran, Bexar County

## Spending to date
$31,400 of $75,000 (42%) has been spent: $18,600 in security deposits, move-in costs and rental assistance paid to landlords, and $12,800 in caseworker time. Spending is on plan. Outcomes are tracked in our HMIS-compatible case-management system and will be verified at 6 and 12 months after exit.

program_report.title: Programme Progress Report: July 1 – September 30, 2026
program_report.content:
# Programme Progress Report: July 1 – September 30, 2026

## Veteran Apprenticeship Readiness Grant — Trades Forward

South Texas Industrial Partners Foundation's $120,000 grant funds instructors, tools and certification fees for Trades Forward, our 14-week pre-apprenticeship in electrical, HVAC and welding at the East Side training workshop.

## Delivered so far
The summer cohort ran from June 29 to October 2, 2026.
- 50 veterans enrolled: 18 in electrical, 17 in HVAC and 15 in welding.
- 41 participants (82%) completed training; 41 earned an OSHA 10 safety certification and 15 earned an EPA Section 608 certification.
- 33 graduates entered registered apprenticeships with partner employers, at an average starting wage of $21.10 an hour.
- 22 volunteer trades mentors supported the cohort, and 9 participants were referred from Homeward Navigation.

## In their words
"Fourteen weeks ago I was sleeping on a friend's couch. Now I'm a first-year electrical apprentice with a pay cheque I can plan around." — Air Force veteran

## Spending to date
$46,500 of $120,000 (39%) has been spent: $31,200 on instructors, $9,800 on tools and protective equipment and $5,500 on certification fees. The autumn cohort begins on October 26, 2026, and spending remains on plan.

outcomes.summary: Would have funded a dedicated women veterans' track within Trades Forward and the Battle Buddy Peer Network.
